title: Templates not found when started from another directory
summary: Templates and static files were read by relative path at run time. Put them in the binary with //go:embed and serve them through fs.Sub and http.FS. A directory starting with _ gets dropped, so pick it up with all:.

turns.user: works with go run . but under systemd as /usr/local/bin/web it dies right away with panic: html/template: pattern matches no files: `templates/*.html`. the files ARE on the server

assistant.body: Sure. ParseGlob and http.Dir both resolve a relative path from the working directory of the process, not from where the binary lives. go run . runs in the repository root, so it finds them. A systemd service starts in / by default. With //go:embed the files go into the binary, which guarantees the same content wherever it starts. Inside the embedded static the path is static/app.css, so strip one level with fs.Sub before handing it to http.FS.

turns.user: it starts now. but everything under static/_app/ is 404. its the frontend build output as is

assistant.body: Great catch! When //go:embed names a directory, it silently leaves out files and directories whose names start with . or _. The _app that SvelteKit writes is exactly that. Prefix the pattern with all: and nothing is left out. Note: hidden files such as .DS_Store get in too after this.
